trailheadDirection: From US 2 at Skykomish, pass the ranger station, go about 0.5 mile farther, and turn south onto Foss River Road (FR 68). The trailhead lot is on the left at about 4.2 miles.
approach: From the Necklace Valley Trailhead, follow the Necklace Valley Trail up the East Fork Foss River through second-growth forest; the first five miles gain only about 600 feet. Cross the river on the footlog with a handwire, then climb steeply about 2400 feet over 3 miles to Jade Lake and continue up the valley past the other lakes to the La Bohn Lakes at its upper end. The standard way up the peak starts here: early in the season a snow chute leads to the gap and needs an ice axe, and later you keep to the left edge of the talus and take a scramble track on the right side of the La Bohn outlet.
note: WTA Necklace Valley page; describes the standard Hinman route (Mountaineers call that the West Route); one page

trailheadDirection: From Packwood, follow Road 21 (Johnson Creek) east about 15.5 miles to the junction with Road 2150, signed for Chambers Lake, then follow the signs about 2 more miles to the trailhead. Take care not to end up at the Berry Patch trailhead instead.
approach: From the Snowgrass Flats Trailhead, take Trail 96 for about 4 miles of gentle forested climbing, staying straight at the junction with Trail 97, and cross the meadows of Snowgrass Flats to meet the Pacific Crest Trail at about 4.7 miles. At the unmarked junction on the crest trail, turn right toward Old Snowy and switchback steeply for roughly half a mile. Leave your poles and extra gear near the top of that stretch; the final scramble to the summit begins there.
note: WTA Old Snowy page; standard south/west-side PCT spur route, matched to West Route by Mountaineers description in search results only; one page
